== Biography ==
Jean was born about 1731. She is the daughter of [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]]. 


== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1499]] is assessed at 95% (proved). The derivative Larne/Kilwaughter chronology explicitly describes Jean 1731 as Hugh’s daughter; Hugh-1499 is the local Ann household account. The possible identification with deceased Jane does not weaken the record-defined daughter’s father.

The 1731 daughter and adult Hugh father; Jean/Jane death identity and Hugh’s origins remain separate.

Next useful test: Compare original MIC/1B/6 baptism with the full monument for Jean/Jane and 8 January 1733.

Source basis already held: [https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html Larne/Kilwaughter congregation register chronology]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


=== Current research ===

The derivative register chronology's Jean, daughter of Hugh, baptised in 1731, may be the Jane named first among Hugh and Ann's eleven deceased children and recorded as dying 8 January 1733. Jean/Jane interchange and chronology support the hypothesis, but the original baptism and full monument must be compared.

This assessment draws on the cited records and public source material.<ref name="ProjectSource1">[https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html Archived Larne/Kilwaughter chronology].</ref><ref name="ProjectSource2">[https://archive.org/stream/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala_djvu.txt Bigger and Hughes, Larne Parish Churchyard inscriptions].</ref><ref name="ProjectSource3">[https://archive.org/details/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/page/47/mode/1up *Ulster Journal of Archaeology*, 2nd series, vol. 6, p. 47].</ref>
